comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C4 regarding limitations of existing approaches. Both evaluations find these background claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes they provide appropriate context through citations, while peer reviewers accept this framing without challenge.

Strong agreement on method development claims C5-C6, C10-C13. Both find the labeling strategy development SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes flow cytometry data and optimization steps, while peer reviewers describe results as 'convincing' and provide 'solid evidence.' Peer result also includes C7 (MHCII-dependence) not in OpenEval R2.

Perfect agreement on functional validation claims C14-C17, C52. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights multiple functional readouts demonstrating preserved T cell function, while peer reviewers note 'extensive array' of studies and find results 'convincing.'

Strong agreement on MHCII-dependence claims C28-C31. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes correlation analysis and knockout experiments as strong evidence, while peer reviewers accept the control strategy without objection. OpenEval R4 also includes C7 not in peer R4.

Agreement on in vivo peptide transfer claims C18-C21, C27, though peer result groups these with additional claims C25-C26, C50. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights flow cytometry and two-photon microscopy data, while peer reviewers note 'surprisingly robust' labeling and 'solid evidence' for cognate-only trogocytosis.

Agreement on iTreg claims C22-C24. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes temporal differences are documented though mechanism unexplored, while peer reviewers accept these supplementary data as consistent with main experiments. Peer result only addresses C23-C24 explicitly.

Agreement on in vivo imaging claims C25-C26. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantified morphological parameters and synapse characteristics, while peer reviewers group these with broader in vivo findings (C19-C21, C27, C50) and praise the robustness of labeling.

Perfect agreement on antigen-specificity claims C32-C36. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes double-pulsing experiments as 'elegant' evidence for precision, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the use of 'multiple non-cognate T cells' as a strength improving robustness.

Agreement on TCR affinity sensitivity claims C37-C41. Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes results match prior characterization but finds C41 somewhat speculative, while peer reviewers accept the variant experiments without challenge, treating the well-characterized variants as solid foundation.

Strong agreement on uncertainty regarding broad comparative and prospective claims C42-C47, C53-C55. Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of head-to-head comparisons and speculative nature of versatility claims, while peer reviewers express reservations about 'ultimate utility' and note 'limited novel biological findings,' emphasizing need for further work.

Disagreement on background labeling limitation claims C48-C49. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, praising transparent acknowledgment and quantitative improvement data. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly identifying this as a weakness that 'may pose problems' for broader applications despite authors' mitigation efforts.

Partial overlap on peptide transfer findings C50-C51. OpenEval finds C50-C51 SUPPORTED with documented temporal persistence. Peer result addresses C50 within broader in vivo findings (C19-C21, C25-C27) and finds it SUPPORTED, praising robustness and potential to reveal fundamental mechanisms.

OpenEval evaluates background context claims C56-C57 as SUPPORTED, noting they justify the new method through comparison to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
OpenEval evaluates established knowledge claim C9 as SUPPORTED, noting it provides important context from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific background claim.
